Topics · One God, one message

Why are religious people sometimes the worst?

What you saw is real. The book describes people who pray and withhold kindness. Judge people, path, or self?

Part 1 of 3

﴿بِسْمِ ٱللَّهِ ٱلرَّحْمَـٰنِ ٱلرَّحِيمِ أَرَءَيْتَ ٱلَّذِى يُكَذِّبُ بِٱلدِّينِ١ فَذَٰلِكَ ٱلَّذِى يَدُعُّ ٱلْيَتِيمَ٢ وَلَا يَحُضُّ عَلَىٰ طَعَامِ ٱلْمِسْكِينِ٣ فَوَيْلٌ لِّلْمُصَلِّينَ٤ ٱلَّذِينَ هُمْ عَن صَلَاتِهِمْ سَاهُونَ٥ ٱلَّذِينَ هُمْ يُرَآءُونَ٦ وَيَمْنَعُونَ ٱلْمَاعُونَ٧﴾

Translation of the meaning

Have you seen the one who denies the Recompense? For that is the one who drives away the orphan And does not encourage the feeding of the poor. So woe to those who pray [But] who are heedless of their prayer[2000] - Those who make show [of their deeds] And withhold [simple] assistance.

Translator's notes

[2000] i.e., the hypocrites who are unconcerned if they miss prayers when no one sees them.

Quran · Al-Ma'un 107:1-7

Translation

But you do see trouble and grief. You consider it to take it into your hand. You help the victim and the fatherless.

Original · Hebrew

רָאִ֡תָה כִּֽי־אַתָּ֤ה ׀ עָ֘מָ֤ל וָכַ֨עַס ׀ תַּבִּיט֮ לָתֵ֪ת בְּיָ֫דֶ֥ךָ עָ֭לֶיךָ יַעֲזֹ֣ב חֵלֶ֑כָה יָ֝ת֗וֹם אַתָּ֤ה ׀ הָיִ֬יתָ עוֹזֵֽר׃

the Psalms · 10:14

World English Bible

This question needs no defence, because what you saw did happen: harm from a clergyman, cruelty from a devout person, show from someone who preaches. This passage says the same before you do. It begins with one who shoves the orphan away and does not urge feeding the poor. Then a startling word: woe to those who pray. It means those who pray distractedly, for show, and refuse the smallest kindness. The book sets the measure in how people are treated.

A question for you

What have you seen most of?

If you sayCruelty in religion's name
ThenThat is the hardest kind, for it comes in a voice claiming mercy. You have every right to measure it by this very text.
If you sayShow and talk without deeds
ThenThat is what the next part takes up directly.
If you sayAbuse of money and power
ThenIt has a question of its own, and the Quran is very clear on it.

Part 2 of 3

﴿يَـٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟ لِمَ تَقُولُونَ مَا لَا تَفْعَلُونَ٢ كَبُرَ مَقْتًا عِندَ ٱللَّهِ أَن تَقُولُوا۟ مَا لَا تَفْعَلُونَ٣﴾

Translation of the meaning

O you who have believed, why do you say what you do not do? Greatly hateful in the sight of Allāh is that you say what you do not do.

Quran · As-Saff 61:2-3

Translation

All things therefore whatever they tell you to observe, observe and do, but don’t do their works; for they say, and don’t do.

Original · Ancient Greek

πάντα οὖν ὅσα ἐὰν εἴπωσιν ὑμῖν ποιήσατε καὶ τηρεῖτε, κατὰ δὲ τὰ ἔργα αὐτῶν μὴ ποιεῖτε, λέγουσιν γὰρ καὶ οὐ ποιοῦσιν.

the Gospel (Matthew) · 23:3

World English Bible

Why does this happen among religious people? One reason: religion gives a person beautiful language, and that language can stand in for the act. One who speaks of mercy often may assume they are merciful. That danger sits close to religious talk. The verse asks believers themselves, face to face: why do you say what you do not do? It calls that hateful to God. So the gap between word and deed is not accepted by the text.

A question for you

What gap between saying and doing do you see, in your circle or in yourself?

Part 3 of 3

World English Bible

﴿لَّيْسَ ٱلْبِرَّ أَن تُوَلُّوا۟ وُجُوهَكُمْ قِبَلَ ٱلْمَشْرِقِ وَٱلْمَغْرِبِ وَلَـٰكِنَّ ٱلْبِرَّ مَنْ ءَامَنَ بِٱللَّهِ وَٱلْيَوْمِ ٱلْـَٔاخِرِ وَٱلْمَلَـٰٓئِكَةِ وَٱلْكِتَـٰبِ وَٱلنَّبِيِّـۧنَ وَءَاتَى ٱلْمَالَ عَلَىٰ حُبِّهِۦ ذَوِى ٱلْقُرْبَىٰ وَٱلْيَتَـٰمَىٰ وَٱلْمَسَـٰكِينَ وَٱبْنَ ٱلسَّبِيلِ وَٱلسَّآئِلِينَ وَفِى ٱلرِّقَابِ وَأَقَامَ ٱلصَّلَوٰةَ وَءَاتَى ٱلزَّكَوٰةَ وَٱلْمُوفُونَ بِعَهْدِهِمْ إِذَا عَـٰهَدُوا۟ ۖ وَٱلصَّـٰبِرِينَ فِى ٱلْبَأْسَآءِ وَٱلضَّرَّآءِ وَحِينَ ٱلْبَأْسِ ۗ أُو۟لَـٰٓئِكَ ٱلَّذِينَ صَدَقُوا۟ ۖ وَأُو۟لَـٰٓئِكَ هُمُ ٱلْمُتَّقُونَ﴾

Translation of the meaning

Righteousness is not that you turn your faces toward the east or the west, but [true] righteousness is [in] one who believes in Allāh, the Last Day, the angels, the Book, and the prophets and gives wealth, in spite of love for it, to relatives, orphans, the needy, the traveler, those who ask [for help], and for freeing slaves; [and who] establishes prayer and gives zakāh; [those who] fulfill their promise when they promise; and [those who] are patient in poverty and hardship and during battle. Those are the ones who have been true, and it is those who are the righteous.

Quran · Al-Baqarah 2:177

Translation

If anyone sues you to take away your coat, let him have your cloak also. Whoever compels you to go one mile, go with him two. Give to him who asks you, and don’t turn away him who desires to borrow from you.

Original · Ancient Greek

καὶ τῷ θέλοντί σοι κριθῆναι καὶ τὸν χιτῶνά σου λαβεῖν, ἄφες αὐτῷ καὶ τὸ ἱμάτιον· καὶ ὅστις σε ἀγγαρεύσει μίλιον ἕν, ὕπαγε μετʼ αὐτοῦ δύο. τῷ αἰτοῦντί σε δός, καὶ τὸν θέλοντα ἀπὸ σοῦ δανίσασθαι μὴ ἀποστραφῇς.

the Gospel (Matthew) · 5:40-42

World English Bible

Does what you saw mean the path itself is false? Logic first: followers behaving badly neither proves nor disproves an idea. Bad doctors do not disprove medicine. The first verse says: theirs is what they earned, and yours what you earned. You will not be asked about what they did. The second defines goodness in faith, giving, keeping promises and patience, not in which way you face. A path is measured by what it teaches. Then the question comes back: what do you want to do?

A question for you

By what should a path be measured, in your view?

If you sayBy its followers
ThenThat view has force: a fruit points to its tree. It meets a question: why treat any one group as the model of its faith?
If you sayBy what it teaches
ThenThen the next step is to read what it teaches for yourself, away from the voice of whoever hurt you.
If you sayI do not want to measure anything now
ThenThat is fine. This door does not close, and there is no hurry.

The same in the other books
